I really had a good time exploring this game in the demo. Now that it is in early access, we have a better vision for the game, and I'm finding my time with it falling flat. I think I just won't click with the design vision of this game. I find rearranging my stickers after each day to be very laborious, and its well worth the time to do that optimization, I just wish it wasn't so loose. Peeling sticker off for free should come at a cost, I want to feel more tension with my deck crafting, not having full freedom to minmax my deck every step of the way. But I see that's not really the vision for the game, customizing is supposed to feel cute and fun. I think I'm just looking for a more engaging decision matrix than this game is going to offer.

Skip this game. The lack of balance and constant crashes are not worth the headaches. There are plenty of deckbuilder roguelikes (this isnt a roguelite, nothing carries between runs.) I've played many difficult deckbuilders and don't mind a challenge, but usually those challenges are fair. This game just tends give the CPU busted decks that you can't recover from and snowballing is an absolute issue. It favors rush decks,mbut most classes involve slow strategies. Meanwhile the CPU will have perfect rush decks by the final week. It would have refunded sooner if I knew just how steep the difficulty cliff was, but this game either deliberately or ignorantly plays it fairly easy until you unlock week three (this unsurprisingly takes a little over 2 hours tomdo) then the computer will literally just sweep you in the first turn (you jnver go first, so younare f'ed.) Just play another game. Maybe they will fix this one, but wait until then at least. Don't let the kiddy visuals and theme fool you. They didn't know what they were doing when they balanced some of these decks.

Ultimately, the game isn't balanced. That's really the major problem. More than half of the stickers available to play pidgeonhole the player into extremely explicit playstyles. This is not inherently a problem, but the game features multiple game-breaking counters to each strategy that the devs have simply chosen with little care to add for free into the enemy decks. The game is primarily a Player vs AI. There is no multiplayer; its a roguelike. Counterspells are feel bad even in the must cutthroat PVP experiences, but I want to make it very clear that Explicitly giving enemies that you will face EVERY SINGLE RUN personal abilities that OBLITERATE half of all the viable stickers in the game is an INSANE design decision. Facing Amit will always face the Robotic dog toy. Facing Min will always result in Dragon every other turn. I forget the boy with the Cat but That certainly isn't fun either. These all hard counter specific deck types, styles of play, and entire functional chunks of the game's library, making the choice to play with these abilities auto-lose conditions. This is a roguelike. You don't get to pick what the RNG gives you.

It's a neat idea, but dear lord is the balance in this game absolutely all over the place. I know that's kinda the idea, with how the game lets you mess with the cards and the effects, but at the end of the day, there is little I can do when the opponents can amass 100 damage on turn one, while others seem to still only use basic cards, even on week 3. I do recommend this game for the aesthetic and variation in fun build potential, but it just feels a little too unbalanced for the time being. Cards often don't do what they say, card-text overlaps with item-descriptions which causes the game to have a panic-attack and simply ignore effects, and I've seen some of the late-game bosses ignore max hand-size limits and even spawn mana out of thin air. I've even seen cases where the opponent just doesn't play a card for 4-5 turns. I suggest giving us more options to get rid of cards when it turns to mid or late game. It does get a little ridiculous how the game expects you to keep a theme to your deck, but still force you to add cards after every day. At some point, it's just not viable to expect me to fill a 15-20 card deck with synergies when I already need so much luck just to pull a sticker that fits the deck-type. Everything you do in this game, is at the mercy of randomness. What stickers you get, what events you get, what the opponent decides to play, if the claw-machine decides to pay out, if you get good stickers in the capsule-machine. There is genuinely no room for any amount of skill, when every aspect of the game, is dictated by RNG. When you can loose the game, on the first mandatory fight of the run, I think we need to step back and reevaluate the balance. The game also expects you to have some sort of counter cards at some point, token removals or counters. But of the game doesn't give one to you, at any point in the run, you are simply at the mercy your opponents RNG. It's just not a fun mechanic, and I hope they change up the progression, the day schedule system, and how the opponents scale, because right now, it's just not fun to roll a dice so often and realise that skill plays such a secondary role in this game. Most of my complaints come from the games hard-mode, where the only viable strategy is to just forfeit until you get an optimal starting scenario. And the amount of sweat and luck needed to beat even the starting opponents is genuinely discouraging. You need to break the game, you need to find infinite combos. There really is no room for experimentation, since there are 200-ish stickers in this game, and there is no way to even somewhat reliably get specific types or grades without just plain RNG, since the game pulls out of the entire pool of stickers, rather than focusing on giving something relating to the chosen deck-type. I'd honestly give it a little more time in the oven while everything gets ironed out. To be completely honest, it's a fine game. The art is charming. The concept is really unique and gameplay is engaging, but it's a little discouraging to get dumpstered on turn 2 on a good run because my opponent just happened to start the round with a stacked hand

Right away, the visuals are what really hooked me. The colours pop, the characters have a lot of expression, and there’s constantly a lot going on without it turning into a true confusing mess. It honestly has way more personality than I expected from a deck builder, and the hand-drawn style is great. I also really like the sticker-based card creation system. Being able to make, tweak, and fully personalise your cards is a really cool feature. That said, I do wish there was a way to save old cards or decks (like exporting them as images with stats, or in a card binder, almost like Pokémon cards.) It’s pretty rough putting effort into a perfect card only to lose it forever after a run goes badly. That said, there are definitely some rough edges. Enemy variety feels pretty... limited. I’ve run into Elias a lot, and it always ends up being the same combat pattern. Spamming that "cancels your next played card" move and cycling through the same small sticker set. His cat card especially feels like it should be a rare rather than something he can just throw out constantly. After a while, bosses start to feel predictable or spammy, and that really takes away from the roguelike feel of the game. Difficulty scaling is also pretty off. By around week 2 (even on relaxed mode), bosses start playing like they’re on full tryhard mode, throwing cards nonstop just to rack up stars. Regular fights are mostly fair, sometimes even easy, but bosses feel like a completely different difficulty tier. If this is what relaxed mode looks like that early, I can’t even imagine what hard mode is like. Astrid, for example, can drop multiple cactus or flower cards at once and then suddenly hit 10+ stars the next turn. It feels like you’re gonna be re-rolling your run just to hope for better RNG. Despite the balance and fairness issues, I’ve still had a good time overall. The charm and visuals do a lot of heavy lifting, and the short story bits between some weeks (where choices actually have positive or negative outcomes) are a nice touch (though I’d like to see those show up more often). Money management also feels pretty fair; I never really struggled to buy what I needed in the shops. Overall, I just hope the devs take a look at balance and variety, because there’s a really solid game here. It just needs some more fine tuning to better support players who want a more relaxed experience rather than a super competitive card game.

This game is definitely fun, and I'm For Real enjoying it, but it's also really, uncomfortably hard. It seems like it was never really balance tested, or maybe all the playtesters were only people who were Extremely Better Than Me. But outside of a couple of degenerate strategies like catlocking people it seems impossible for every archetype to get past week 2 much less win, which seems to me to be oddly antithetical to the point of a TCG deckbuilder, that some archetypes simply cannot compete no matter how lucky you get with the extra parts you graft onto them. I will edit this review when they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the balancing.

游戏本身很好玩，但是平衡性确实一般，有几个针对性很强的贴纸，玩家拿了没啥用，因为每个敌人流派不一样，你拿了也就只能针对很少的敌人，其他大部分时间都是废纸，但是这些针对卡出现在敌人手里，你玩的卡组刚好又被针对的时候，比吃了一坨还难受，比如有个卡组专门叠虫和蛇，慢慢叠多了，强度越来越高最后赢得胜利，有个小孩有个红龙卡一键清屏，困难难度这货卡组甚至有两张这卡，你玩虫卡组遇到这货基本很难赢，但是这个游戏三层打完，遇敌基本上是每个敌人都至少有一次，你百分百会遇到甚至可以一局遇到他好几次，你用这种叠标记的卡组巨难打，然后游戏十个卡组有七个是标记卡组，导致你玩这些卡组想通关最高难度，清一色是转型别的打法才能通关。 我已经把全卡组最高难度通关了，我可以直说，平衡性就是一坨，而且是需要大改的那种，强力贴纸巨强，有两个贴纸，拿到就能保送最高难度通关，效果都是同一个卡贴纸越多给的星星越多，强到可以一卡叠一千星费用还低，四倍伤害瞬间击杀对面倒欠我几千血，弱贴纸那就多到没法数，困难难度敌人叠星速度巨快，第一周boss你就可以见到敌人一回合叠30星，还玩那种一费4星的贴纸根本赢不了，然鹅这游戏1费4星已经算优质过渡贴纸了，困难难度很多卡组不抓过渡卡游戏第二个小怪都过不了，我不知道制作组测试游戏难度的时候，有没有考虑过那些垃圾卡组的初始强度，残疾卡组一大堆，一费4星贴纸很多，但是你一费4鱼，还要再花1费把鱼转星，而且还是1比1转，2费4星，简直拉到没法玩，1转2的贴纸就一种，而且稀有度还高很少遇到，甚至就这还有严苛的使用条件，直接埋了吧，恐龙卡组就更蠢了，把卡抓手里三回合才有效果，这效果可以说从游戏开局垃圾到最后，打第一个怪都要拼劲全力，还有砖石卡组，别的卡组打到第二周第三周都开始寻求效率翻倍的能力了，砖石还在抽一打一叠标记，标记成型速度比虫卡组还慢，而且一标记一星，不是哥们，困难第三周有的敌人一回合就100星，你还在一费一标记一星，等你叠起来黄花菜都凉透了，制作组自己来表演一下，中途不允许大改卡组构筑的情况，比如鱼卡组就一直玩鱼，恐龙卡组就一直抓恐龙贴纸作为主体输出，不能中途抓一堆车贴纸换车输出，你用这几个卡组通关困难难度给我看看，打的过吗，真的测试过不同流派的整体平衡吗，车和音乐卡组无脑强，我闭着眼抓都能通关，有的卡组开局打第一个怪都汗流浃背了 说实话，这游戏体验一下简单难度随便玩玩就行了，深入到数值方面就真的没眼看，我前面还只说了贴纸的不平衡，这游戏还有玩具（就是其他游戏的遗物或者说藏品）的不平衡，事件收益的不平衡，而且稀有度高的贴纸非常难遇到等多方面的问题，看看别人视频再考虑这游戏要不要入 2025/11/11

It's still really early on for me... and I do not hate this. But I do find it very disappointing. Two main reasons: 1. The synergies. The game has obvious synergies. The problem is that they are not well thought through and fleshed out. They are skin deep and at least some seem to be worse than simply grinding stars. Big problem for me, as synergies are the true joy and draw of this genre. 2. You spend 75%-80% of your time not dueling. The biggest issue is probably the card construction process. It is sooo clunky. To really see what you want to do you need to be able to see most of your cards at the same time. The interface is clearly not made to do this. It's a real pain. Strategizing is cool and important. But it needs to be streamlined so we can spend our time doing what we came to do. Maybe my experience will change. But compared to other games of the same genre, I really find this lacking. Maybe it's not targeted for serious deck builder fans.

This game is very charming and I really, really, REALLY want to love it. However there are some very major issues with this but it's expected since it's in early access. I believe it needs more toys which function like passive abilities since the selection given is very limited (not to mention you can only have 4 at a time) plus playing this game on Hard is basically unfeasible. You have mid to bad cards while the enemies have the best cards in the world making for a VERY unenjoyable experience. This game is VERY reliant on good RNG to get anywhere in the game and the Hard difficulty basically multiplies this issue by tenfold. Once you beat this game on Normal I'd suggest just putting it down or continue playing on Normal since Hard mode is just unfair and tedious. Some starting Decks are more stupidly powerful compared to others so it's an uphill battle to play certain ones (like set up decks for example) and sometimes it's just outright impossible which is compounded by enemies that have the absolute PERFECT deck compared to your deck which is reliant on RNG. This game also needs more options to pick up cards and destroy cards (more so destroy cards) so you can curate your deck even more. Overall, this game feels like it has a lot of potential and I really want to enjoy it but these issues especially with the stupidly unfair difficulty of hardmode makes it difficult to enjoy. PLEASE fix these issues and I still recommend this game to casual enjoyers of deckbuilders but I'm going to have to give this game a negative review since it's just not fun at a certain point due to these issues. Once these issues are fixed I'll change my review but until then....

游戏画风特别可爱，贴纸自由组合也特别萌，NPC也特别萌，而且玩法也是肉鸽卡牌游戏，自己组合词条印卡，总体来说前期游玩体验也还是很好的。但是当后期难度提高，玩家不得不考虑卡组强度的时候，会发现在词条平衡与卡组数量等方面严重欠缺考量。 难度方面，给敌人带黑猫加幸运的卡，这个设计是认真的吗？ 敌人永远先手，玩了一个多小时的存档在后期遇到黑猫小伙，先手一张黑猫加25%幸运，连续触发了五次，黑猫的效果是让对手下一张打出的卡无效，但是费用照扣。轮到我的回合直接五张卡无效，后续敌人又一直出黑猫，我到结束游戏了都没成功打出一张卡 。 先不提这种直接影响游戏平衡的扔卡设计很搞人心态，当构筑叠层流派的时候还有直接烧代币的掀桌对手，辛辛苦苦叠了一整把的层数被一张巨龙贴纸全烧了。就这一个黑猫贴纸一个巨龙贴纸的设计，就注定了叠层卡组和高费卡组玩不了，游戏是好游戏，但是词条平衡真的很糟心，运营半天被一张卡搞输了，负反馈真的很大。 如果要玩，请注意，玩高费别找黑猫小孩打架，玩叠层别找恐龙服小孩打架。 总的来说休闲游玩还是很值得一试，画风很萌，放轻松来游玩，像个小孩一样把所有强大的贴纸贴到一张卡上，吓死和你对战的朋友。

I love this game but in it's current state, it's far too unbalanced. Depending on which build you're using, some opponents, especially the final opponent of week 3 make the game entirely unplayable. Challenging opponents can be fun, but there's a difference between challenging and simply unfair. If an opponent gets 100-200 stars in a turn, unless you're playing a perfect deck, is incredibly difficult to get the luck of the draw to even recover. I hope that this game sees a lot of rebalancing updates prior to it's actual release because it truly can be fun.

To be clear, this is not a bad game. Its super cute, and has a very compelling and addicting loop. When you first start. But after sinking some hours in the problems start to appear. The RNG is brutal. You can often just get NOTHING during events. The things you use to improve your deck. Which will often lead to your loss thanks to enemies decks growing in power faster than your own, sporting multiple rare stickers where you may have a whole 1 to your name. To compound this problem, the game forces you to keep adding cards to your deck forcing deck bloat. ( I do not hate this idea in a vacuum, because it keeps you making cards which is good, but it only adds to the problems listed above) In addition to this, the seemingly optimal way to play and or beat this is an unfun way to play. Slam all your best stickers onto a single card and try to One turn kill your opponent so they don't have time to play their BS. Which is fun the first few times you do it. But after battle 10 you will be turning the game speed to max and yawning as you wait for the animations to finish for your guaranteed victory. This strategy also ruins the cute cozy card designing aspect of the game. As instead of taking time to make cards you enjoy the look of, you slap every sticker in the world onto a card to create something you realistically would see sticking out of your deck from the sheer added mass. ( and to be fair, OTK I think should be allowed for those who want to pursue it, but it likely should not be THIS easy to make or optimal, but due to the RNG other strategies are harder to pull off and are less reliable.) I think this game has real potential and is already 80% of the way there. But its flaws really started to grind on me after hours 4-6. I played mostly out of spite to see "The End" and now have little desire to play more at this time. Unlike how I feel about say, slay the spire.

This game is extremely cute with a lot of charm, and I really enjoyed getting to try it. However, even with a lot more content to explore, I find my interest waning, as the gameplay leaves me more and more disappointed. Essentially, the battles are far too solitaire for my liking. On each player's turn, they put out cards that give them stars, and whoever has more stars gets points towards winning the game. There's a tiny bit of counterplay possible, but a lot is rather deck agnostic and generally isn't necessary (I've yet to see opponents use a meaningful amount of it). Essentially, I found myself checking out of whatever the opponent was doing as I just continued to repeat using the same deck with the same strategy, just slightly stronger, for basically every single of the over 15 matches in the run. It's easy enough that if you're good at this kind of game, it's not too hard to steamroll every match on normal. I heard hard is unfair, but I don't find the gameplay fun enough to be interested in trying it. I know it's in early access, so perhaps things could change, but my issues seem to be rather foundational to how the game plays. Others may like it more, I just really need more interacton between players in my card games.

I'm going to echo what several others have said: it's a super cute game and the core gameplay is solid and entertaining. The sticker system feels unique and adds a lot of customization. However, the game feels very unbalanced at the moment; if you're unlucky you can get absolutely shafted with stickers and toys, while the opponents steadily increase in difficulty regardless. And even if you do get a good deck going, it's very easy to run into opponents that completely counter your entire playstyle. Say you have built a deck focused on tokens like bugs and snakes, then you run into an opponent that converts the bugs you play into energy for himself, and steals your snakes. Continue to play the cards you have built and you will just feed the opponent more energy and stars while he continues stealing from you. And apparently, the stickers that protect your tokens do not seem to work against stealing, which feels both counterintuitive and unfair. So for now, it's a no, but I'd absolutely be willing to try the game out again if the balancing and RNG are properly adressed.

This game is a genuinely wonderful creation, its art is chamring and the gameplay is fun. Until you unlock everything. This used to not be a problem, but the devs have recently added a number of new sticker packs, of which all the stickers get added to the general pool that you encounter in your runs. Here's the problem, about 90% of all stickers are just.. bad in various forms. Most of them are okay provided you're following a specific deck's strategy (which RNG biases you toward if playing that particular deck), but these stickers are otherwise utterly worthless when you're not doing that strategy. In addition, you can't easily pivot into another sticker strategy due to a lack of synergy pieces between strategies, and the ones they did add after people made mention of this are so laughably bad, they simply make the already overbloated pool of stickers so much worse. Let's put it this way, I used to be able to play this game semi decently on hard mode, now I can't even finish a run on normal mode because the chances of me encountering any decent base cards, and especially card draw, are so horrenously low, it's practically guaranteed to you'll have a deck that struggles by the endgame. This is no longer the game I fell in love with, and it could be resolved if they just allowed a way to ban packs before your run. Edit: In hope for the current changes the developers have announced which address the issues I mentioned, I've changed this review to positive. Though buyer do be beware, these changes are yet to come. Edit 2: The update was alright, it didn't solve much of anything. Runs are still horrible on several decks, the game is still full of frankly useless stickers, and every run is a matter of RNG as to whether or not you encounter enough candy or draw stickers. This wouldnt' be a problem if you could reliably thin out your deck, but as it stands now, the game is great but frustrating. It doesn't feel like your deckbuilding choices make a lot of difference when your run is just screwed.

I want to preface my review by stating that this game is in early access, and though it has some very real issues it ultimately can be a fun game with lots of variety, an adorable art style, and a very addicting gameplay loop. There is very real potential for a solid game here, but there are some very real pain points that need to be addressed. Playing through the game and unlocking things was fun at first, but the cracks were pretty apparent early on and they grew into gaping chasms as I progressed. Here are some of my pain points that really ruined the experience for me: >The over-reliance on random elements is a problem. Far, far too much of success in a run depends on randomness that players are given few if any tools to mitigate. Missing key stickers that your deck needs to survive against counters, events that give you nothing (or worse, hurt you), runs with no toys, runs with no recycles, runs with too many flea markets and claw machines, runs where you're forced to pick between two opponents that counter your deck. All too common, all too frustrating. >Because of aforementioned RNG, difficulty is all over the place. Easy is, well, easy. Normal and Hard are ???. Certain decks (Hi Detectives and Fish) can struggle to make it through Normal while others (Hi Music) will pretty consistently make it to the end of Hard. Opponent difficulty is all over the place with some of the regular battles being MUCH harder than the "Super tough" ones. Don't even get me started about some encounters being borderline unwinnable if your deck gets countered. >On that note, battles feel too frontloaded. Generated stars persist between rounds, so it's very easy to fall behind and stay behind, especially with one of the slower rolling decks. Cards that can steal stars and tokens from the opponent are rare and only one clears the board. These cards feel essential at higher difficulties and indicate bad game design. The sudden death mechanic is arbitrary and punishes attrition-based strategy. >The forced card bloat is just awful. Recycling isn't enough and there's a reason why most games in the genre have adding cards as optional. The grindy, uphill battle against AI that always has fewer cards and better stickers than you can wear very thin. The game often forces the player into dumping all of their good stickers onto a few good cards and having a pile of worthless/empty ones instead of making an entire coherent functioning deck. >Unlocking new decks bloats the sticker pool, which actively hurts the performance of some decks. >With all the factors that can and do kill runs (many completely independent of player choice) losing the time and effort investment hurts. It'd be nice if there were a way to purchase good cards from previous runs, or have painful losses mitigated by better RNG in the next run. In all, I can't recommend the game in its current state unless you're a fan of lotteries that masquerade as choice-driven roguelikes. With proper balance and QOL I do think this game has lots of potential. However it is competing with the likes of other more polished deck-builders like Balatro, Slay the Spire (1 and 2) and Monster Train (1 and 2). I'd recommend any of those over this game for a better experience.

It's fine for an early access, and the aesthetics, music, ui, are great. However, the core gameplay meta, assuming you want to win, even on normal, is quite poor. ------ While the game initially presents itself as a hee-hee happy sticker card game, the actual meta of it, is sickening, as alluded to by the final boss. I do not recommend Hard mode, where enemies are arbitrarily spamming foils for free (every single card had candies). The second worst encounter is the pastry chef girl, Laura, as she slowly accumulates 200 candies, popping a few hundred stars whenever she swaps, and re-popping with her blossoms for another hundred. Since she averages the candies with you, you can't even steal them. You can't even burn them all because she generates them so quickly, unless you are running some insane 40+ cost brick. Fortunately, the final boss, just spams a steal 7 candy + discard 2 combo, steals tokens, superior scaling, and has dragons. It was quite literally unplayable, despite me having 20 candies and 4 cards, all wiped within a single turn. -------------- To counter them, I had to run tech cards, like the steal 1 token stack card or several dragons to chain reset turns after securing a small lead. Every round is just gambling my way to victory. Every card shop, hoping for a core combo piece, free energy, free draw, just so you can pray to RNG-sus, that the final boss didn't instantly wipe your hand AND energy away. Alternatively, you could stack some giga knight 20 candy combo to just one-shot every encounter. -------------- Additionally, until the devs add the ability to at least trim some of the pack unlocks, or significantly better ways to reroll for cards, the game genuinely gets more unplayable with each unlock.

My Card is Better Than Your Card is such a wholesome and fun little card game to play. While it is still in Early Access and has some kinks and bugs to work out, I do appreciate that it feels like a whole experience and I've been able to go through multiple runs already without any issues. What I like: * The ability to create your own cards using really cute stickers. You can make the silliest cards and I love that I can be a little creative during this part of the game. * The decks can be so interesting to make and I love combining different cards to figure out what works the best for my play style. * Even though the game features kids playing a card game, it is NOT easy to beat and does not get boring. You definitely have to strategize if you want to beat up some of the kids since some of them really have wiped the floor with me. * The visuals are a cotton candy sugar rush feast for my inner child. Everything is just so vibrant and I love the animations of the kids playing a card and reacting to each other. I also love the different tokens that can be on the board, such as school of fish swimming around and bugs flying around until a snake eats them. Everything is just so fun (albeit probably a little overstimulating for some I'm sure) * I like that you can pick from one of two schedules that has a variety of different activities for you to do such as beat up opponents, trade stickers, dig in the sandbox, play gachapon, and other activities to gain more stickers and money. What I wish were different: * I don't really have anything that I want to be different right now I think this game is for you if you are a fan of deckbuilders or if you're looking for cute visuals and also a challenge. It might get boring if you play multiple rounds in a row, but I found that it is most engaging whenever I play for short bursts every now and then.
